categoryName: OTC pharmacy — analgesics, antipyretics, cold/cough, antacid, antiseptic, ORS, laxatives, antifungal, band-aid

skuLines.examples: Crocin Advance 500mg (20 tab), Calpol 500 (15 tab), Dolo 500 (15 tab), Pacimol 500 (IPCA)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10 / 15 / 20 tablets; also loose-strip sale
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Jul-Sep (post-monsoon viral/dengue wave) and Nov-Feb (hill winter flu)
skuLines.marginBand: 16% on DPCO-scheduled paracetamol (fixed retailer margin); 20-25% on non-scheduled brands
skuLines.notes: The single highest-unit SKU in the whole category. Needs a retail drug licence (Form 20/21) + registered pharmacist. Shelf life 24-36 months. Sell by batch — a recall must be traceable. Buy 3-4 months' cover, not 12: expiry write-off beats a stock-out here.

skuLines.examples: Dolo 650 (Micro Labs, 15 tab), Calpol 650, Leemol 650 (Leeford), P 650 (Apex), Lanol ER 650
skuLines.seasonality: Same as 500mg; the 650 is what adults actually ask for by name
skuLines.notes: Stock TWO tiers deliberately: Dolo 650 for brand-askers and one generic 650 at half the price. Jan Aushadhi price-anchoring (16,912 Kendras, 2,110 molecules as of Jun-2025) makes a ₹32 branded strip look expensive to a resident who has seen the generic.

skuLines.examples: Calpol 250mg strawberry 60ml, Crocin 240mg DS mixed fruit 60ml, P-250 (Apex) 60ml
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks with dorm/creche viral waves — Jul-Sep and Dec-Feb
skuLines.notes: Married-staff families with small children make this non-negotiable. Glass bottle, freight-fragile on the Rajgarh hill road — order in the supplier's own carton, never loose. Do NOT store in an unheated godown in winter: suspensions separate/freeze below 0°C. Stock both strengths; parents get the dose wrong otherwise.

skuLines.examples: Crocin Drops 15ml (100mg/ml), Calpol 100 Drops, P-Drops (Apex), Metacin drops
skuLines.notes: Different SKU from the 60ml suspension — infants under 2 need the concentrated dropper. Low volume, high consequence: a family with a feverish baby and 40 km of night hill road has nowhere else. One-line stock-out policy: never zero.

skuLines.examples: Combiflam (Sanofi), Brufen 400, Nicip Plus (Cipla), Flexon
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; sports-term and winter joint-pain lift
skuLines.notes: The go-to for sprains, dental pain and period pain. Counsel 'after food' — NSAID on an empty student stomach drives the acidity sale you then also make. Not for babies.

skuLines.examples: Saridon (Bayer), Disprin / Disprin Plus, Anacin, Nimulid MD
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10; also 4-tab and single-tab sachets
skuLines.seasonality: Exam blocks and term-end; year-round otherwise
skuLines.marginBand: 12-20% (FMCG-style trade margin, Saridon is heavily distributed)
skuLines.notes: The ₹2-5 loose-tablet impulse buy. Highest bill-frequency item in the lane and a reason a student walks in at all. Keep on the counter, not the back shelf.

skuLines.line: Topical NSAID pain gel and spray
skuLines.examples: Volini gel 30/75/100g, Volini spray 15/42/100g, Moov ointment 30/50g, Dynapar QPS spray, Moov Active spray
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov-Feb (cold-weather joint and back pain) plus school/university sports terms
skuLines.notes: A residential school + university means constant sprains, and 5,000 people with no physio. Stock the small spray (₹64-77) as the volume SKU and one 100g for staff households. Spray cans are pressurised — hill freight is fine, but do not store near a heater.

skuLines.line: Ayurvedic pain balm, oil and rub
skuLines.examples: Zandu Balm 8/25ml, Amrutanjan Pain Balm, Iodex Double Power 40g, Tiger Balm, Kesari Jivan / Mahanarayan oil
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp Oct-Mar peak in a cold hill location
skuLines.marginBand: 20-40% (Ayurvedic proprietary carries the best margin in this lane)
skuLines.notes: Legally an Ayurvedic proprietary medicine, not an allopathic drug — sellable under an Ayurvedic licence, which is far easier to hold than Form 20/21. Highest-margin, lowest-regulation block in the whole category: over-index here.

skuLines.line: Pain relief patch, plaster and roll-on
skuLines.examples: Volini Roll-On 5/10ml, Dr. Ortho pain relief patch, Salonpas, Tiger Balm patch, Liveasy pain relief patch
skuLines.notes: Volini's ₹31 clove-mint headache roll-on is a genuine impulse SKU for a student wallet. Patches sell to staff who don't want smell on their clothes at work. Small tail — one facing each, don't build depth.

skuLines.examples: Cofsils Wet Cough SF 100ml, Zedex 100ml (Dr Reddy's), Viscodyne SF 100ml, Norvent-D 100ml
skuLines.seasonality: Very strong Oct-Mar; second wave Jul-Sep with the monsoon
skuLines.notes: Cough/cold is the number-one category in a cold hill township with dormitories. Sugar-free is now the default ask. Codeine- and chlorpheniramine-containing syrups are Schedule H/H1 and must be Rx-logged — keep those behind the counter and separate from the freely-sellable ones.

skuLines.examples: Codistar DC 100ml (Mankind), Benadryl DR, Alkof Junior 60ml (paediatric), Torex
skuLines.notes: Distinct clinical need from wet cough — carry both or you will sell the wrong one. Keep a paediatric 60ml (Alkof Junior ₹75 MRP) for the families cohort; children's dosing on an adult bottle is where harm happens.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Honitus 100ml, Himalaya Koflet 100ml, Zandu Ayurvedic Cough Syrup 100ml, Baidyanath Kasamrit, Kofol 200ml
skuLines.notes: Ayurvedic licence, not Form 20/21. In a Sikh institution the herbal line is often actively preferred over allopathic syrup — and it carries double the margin. Check for alcohol content: some Ayurvedic tonics are self-generated-alcohol asava/arishta preparations, which will be a problem in this township. Read the label before you list it.

skuLines.examples: Sinarest, D-Cold Total, Cheston Cold, Vicks Action 500 Advance, Coldact
skuLines.notes: Contains phenylephrine/chlorpheniramine + paracetamol. Several of these are Schedule H — sale must be against a prescription and entered in the register. Volume is real but so is the compliance load; this is a licence-required block.

skuLines.examples: Cetzine 10mg, Alerid, Okacet (cetirizine); Levocet / Xyzal (levocetirizine); Allegra 120
skuLines.seasonality: Feb-Apr pollen and Jul-Sep damp/dust-mite spikes; year-round base
skuLines.notes: Cheapest genuinely useful drug on the shelf. Also the fallback for insect bites, urticaria and dorm dust allergy. Cetirizine is Schedule H in India despite being sold casually — the register entry matters if ARY holds a licence.

skuLines.examples: Otrivin Oxy 10ml, Otrivin Advance Menthol 10g, Nasivion Classic Adult 10ml, Naselin 10ml
skuLines.notes: Counsel a 5-day maximum — rebound congestion from over-use is common and a captive customer will just keep buying. Small, light, high value per gram: ideal item to carry deep buffer stock on, since freight cost is negligible.

skuLines.line: Saline nasal drops / spray — baby and adult
skuLines.examples: Nasoclear 0.65% 20ml, Otrivin Baby Saline 20ml, Nasivion S 0.65% 10ml, Naselin Saline 20ml
skuLines.notes: The only nasal product safe for infants — a blocked baby in a cold hill winter is a weekly event across ~5,000 residents with young staff families. Cheap, no side effects, high repeat. Never substitute an adult decongestant here.

skuLines.examples: Vicks VapoRub 10/25/50/105ml, Vicks VapoRub Xtra Strong 25/50ml, Amrutanjan Cold Rub
skuLines.marginBand: 12-20% (Vicks is a low-margin, high-rotation FMCG line)
skuLines.notes: Registered as an Ayurvedic proprietary medicine, so it sells outside Form 20/21 — which is why every hill kirana carries it. The ₹48 10ml jar is the volume SKU for students; the 105ml is a staff-family purchase. Build 8-10 weeks of winter cover before the first October order round; this is the item you most regret being out of in January.

skuLines.line: Steam inhaler, vaporiser and inhalant capsules
skuLines.examples: Karvol Plus capsules, Vicks Inhaler stick, Vicks Steam Inhaler, Dr Trust / PharmEasy vaporizer, Nilgiri (eucalyptus) oil 15ml
skuLines.packSizes: inhaler stick 0.5ml; capsules 10s; vaporizer 1 unit; oil 10/15/25ml
skuLines.notes: Steam is the first-line home remedy in a cold damp climate and needs no licence for the device or the oil. The ₹46 keychain inhaler is a student impulse item. Stock 2-3 vaporizers in October, not in April — the device is a one-off purchase per household, so it saturates.

skuLines.examples: Strepsils 120s/288s jar, Cofsils Orange/Ginger-Lemon/Mulethi 10s and 120s jar, Himalaya Koflet-H 6s, Vicks Cough Drops
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 6 / 10; jar of 50 / 100 / 120 / 288; loose single lozenge
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Mar peak; year-round base from teachers and singers
skuLines.notes: Buy the 120/288 jar and sell loose at ₹2-3 — that is the single best margin move in the category and it matches how a student actually buys. Teaching staff (all-day talking) are a steady non-seasonal base. Keep at the till.

skuLines.examples: Betadine Gargle 100ml, Hexidine mouthwash 160ml, Colgate Plax, Tantum / Zytee throat spray
skuLines.notes: Povidone-iodine gargle needs a drug licence; the cosmetic mouthwashes do not. Modest volume — one facing each. Also the item to point a sore-throat customer at instead of an antibiotic they don't need.

skuLines.examples: Digene 200/400ml, Gelusil MPS SF 200/400ml, Polycrol Xpress 450ml, Diovol SF mint/mango 170ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; lifts during exam blocks and festival/langar eating
skuLines.notes: Mess-food acidity across a university population is a permanent demand floor. Sugar-free is now the standard SKU — carry SF as the default and regular only if asked. Heavy and liquid: 400ml glass/PET bottles are the worst freight-to-value ratio in the lane, so favour the tablet and sachet formats for buffer stock.

skuLines.examples: Digene tablets 15s, Gelusil MPS mint 15s, Diovol Plus tablets, Mucaine chewable
skuLines.notes: The pocketable format that actually moves in a hostel — a student will not carry a 200ml bottle. Gelusil MPS 15s at ₹27 MRP is the price-point SKU. Sells loose extremely well.

skuLines.examples: Eno Regular / Orange / Lemon 5g sachet and 100g bottle, Gas-O-Fast Jeera / Ajwain / Lemon 5g
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes around festivals, langar and wedding season
skuLines.marginBand: 15-25% on the bottle; 25-40% when you break a 24-pack and sell singles
skuLines.notes: The ₹8-10 sachet is the cheapest thing in the category and one of the highest-frequency. Buy the 24-sachet carton, hang a strip at the counter. Gas-O-Fast's jeera/ajwain variants outsell plain Eno in North Indian hill markets — stock both flavour families.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Pudin Hara pearls/liquid, Hajmola, Zandu Pancharishta 450ml, Himalaya Gasex 100s, Unienzyme 15s, Ajmal Sat Isabgol
skuLines.packSizes: Pudin Hara 10 pearls / 30ml; Hajmola 120 tab bottle; Pancharishta 200/450ml; Gasex 50/100 tab
skuLines.notes: Best margin-to-regulation ratio in the digestive block: Ayurvedic licence only, and it is what most residents will ask for first. Hajmola is effectively a confectionery impulse SKU — put it at the till, not the pharmacy shelf. Check the Pancharishta label for self-generated alcohol before listing it in this township.

skuLines.examples: Enterogermina 5ml vials, Darolac sachet, Vibact DS, Sporlac DS, Econorm 250mg sachet
skuLines.notes: Pairs with every ORS sale during a monsoon diarrhoea run — and it is the honest thing to sell instead of an antibiotic. Live-culture products want storage below 25°C: fine in a hill store, but do not put them next to a heater in winter. Watch expiry, potency is dated.

skuLines.examples: Pan 40 / Pantocid 40mg, Omez 20mg, Rantac 150, Aciloc 150, Pantocid DSR
skuLines.notes: Prescription-only (Schedule H) — NOT an OTC line, even though residents will ask for it by name. Stock this only if ARY runs a licensed counter with a registered pharmacist and a sale register. Long-term PPI use is also a real harm, so this is a dispense-against-script item, not a shelf item.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Antiseptic Liquid 125/250/550/1000ml, Savlon Antiseptic Liquid 100/500ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; lifts Jul-Sep (monsoon hygiene) and at school-session start
skuLines.notes: Dormitories, kitchens, two canteens and a school infirmary all consume this. Carry the 1L for institutional/warden purchase and the 125ml for households. Note it is licensed as a drug in India, not a cosmetic, and attracts 18% GST unlike most medicines at 5% — price it separately, do not blanket-apply the medicine rate.

skuLines.line: Antiseptic / antibiotic wound cream and ointment
skuLines.examples: Soframycin Skin Cream 30g, Neosporin powder/ointment, Savlon Antiseptic Cream 20/50g, Betadine ointment 15/20g, T-Bact
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes with sports terms and monsoon skin infections
skuLines.notes: Soframycin at ₹54 is the workhorse: a residential school generates grazes daily. Framycetin and mupirocin are antibiotics — Schedule H, so they need the licence and the register. Betadine/povidone-iodine is the one to push for dirty wounds and needs no antibiotic-stewardship worry.

skuLines.examples: Betadine 5% solution 100ml, Cipladine 5% solution/ointment 20/30g, Wokadine
skuLines.notes: First-line for a contaminated cut, which on a hill campus is most cuts. Stains cloth — tell the buyer. 500ml bottle for the school infirmary and canteens as an institutional line; 100ml for households.

skuLines.line: Surgical spirit, hydrogen peroxide and chlorhexidine
skuLines.examples: Surgical spirit 100/400ml, Hydrogen peroxide 6% 100ml, Savlon Hexi Scrub, Sterillium hand rub
skuLines.notes: Institutional buyers (infirmary, canteens, warehouse first-aid) drive this more than households. Spirit is flammable and, in a Sikh institution, worth stocking in the clearly-labelled surgical section rather than anywhere it reads as a consumable. Peroxide degrades in light — dark bottle, cool shelf, and don't over-order.

skuLines.examples: Nebasulf powder 10g, Soframycin dusting powder 120g, Cicatrin, Zeet dusting powder
skuLines.notes: Genuinely useful in a heavy-monsoon climate where a wound stays damp and a cream traps moisture. Antibiotic-containing versions are Schedule H. Slow but steady — one facing, don't build depth.

skuLines.examples: Burnol 20g, Silverex Ionic gel 25g, Soframycin, Liveasy Burns Cream 20g
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; kitchen-scald peak in winter and around festival cooking
skuLines.notes: Two canteens, a langar culture and hundreds of staff kitchens make scalds routine. Silver sulphadiazine is Rx; Burnol is freely sellable. This is a low-turnover, must-never-be-zero item — the nearest alternative is 30-50 km of hill road at the exact moment it is needed.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Instant Hand Sanitizer 50/200ml, Lifebuoy, Savlon Hand Sanitizer, Himalaya PureHands
skuLines.seasonality: Jul-Sep and any outbreak week; structurally lower than 2021-22 levels
skuLines.notes: Demand has normalised well below the pandemic peak — resist over-stocking. Alcohol-based content is worth a quiet check with the institution before you make it a hero SKU in a Sikh township; non-alcohol formats exist. Institutional sale (school, hostels, canteens) is the real volume, not walk-in.

skuLines.examples: Electral 21.8g (FDC), Prolyte ORS 21g, Walyte 22g, ORS Insta 21.8g, Ranbaxy ORS 21.8g
skuLines.seasonality: Hard Jul-Sep monsoon peak (water contamination), second lift Apr-Jun
skuLines.notes: The single most important public-health SKU on this list. 5,000 residents on one water source in heavy monsoon means a diarrhoea run can hit dozens of people in a week, and the road out is unreliable. Powder, not tetrapak, is what you stockpile: light, non-perishable, 24-36 month shelf life, and you are not paying hill freight on water. Insist on WHO-formula labelling.

skuLines.examples: Electral 4.4g (orange, lychee, shikanji, mango), Walyte 4.4g, Liveasy ORS 4.4g
skuLines.seasonality: Jul-Sep peak; also sports/heat use Apr-Jun
skuLines.notes: The ₹4 price point is what a student actually buys, and flavours matter for compliance in children. One glass per sachet removes the dosing error that makes home-made ORS dangerous. Break-bulk from a 50-sachet box and hang at the counter.

skuLines.examples: ORSL / ORSL Plus 200ml, Prolyte ORS Nimbu Paani and Mixed Fruit 200ml, Electral Plus, Walyte RTD 200ml
skuLines.notes: Convenience format — sells to whoever is already ill and doesn't want to mix. Thin margin, bulky, and you pay hill freight on water: carry a shallow facing, not a pallet, and keep the sachets as your actual buffer stock. Note the 2025 regulatory push against sugary drinks marketed as 'ORS' — stock only genuine WHO-formula labelled product.

skuLines.examples: Glucon-D (regular, Nimbu Pani, Tangy Orange) 100g/450g/1kg, Glucose-D, Dextrose powder
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Jun peak; sports and exam-season base
skuLines.notes: Not a substitute for ORS and should never be sold as one — glucose alone lacks the sodium. Sits half in grocery, half in pharmacy; decide which counter owns it so it isn't double-stocked. Hygroscopic: cakes hard in a damp monsoon godown, so keep it sealed and off the floor.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Nature Care Isabgol, Sat-Isabgol (Telephone brand) 100/200g, Softovac SF 250/450g, Naturolax
skuLines.seasonality: Winter lift (low fluid intake in cold weather); year-round base
skuLines.notes: The safest laxative to hand an elderly resident, and the one to recommend before any stimulant. Bulky and hygroscopic — absorbs monsoon moisture and clumps, so store sealed and rotate. The elderly cohort here buys it as a standing monthly repeat: worth a pre-picked refill list.

skuLines.examples: Dulcoflex 5mg 15s (bisacodyl), Cremalax, Laxopeg, Gerbisa
skuLines.notes: Cheap, effective, easy to over-use — counsel short-term use only. Dulcoflex at ₹19 for 15 tablets is the price anchor. Tiny footprint, long shelf life: no reason ever to be out.

skuLines.line: Ayurvedic laxative churna, granules and vati
skuLines.examples: Zandu Nityam vati 10s/30s and churna 100g, Pet Saffa granules 60/120/200g, Kayam Churna, Baidyanath Triphala churna 100/500g
skuLines.notes: Ayurvedic licence only, best margins in the laxative block, and the format most of this population trusts. Triphala also cross-sells as a general wellness item. Churna is loose powder — moisture is the enemy in a monsoon hill store, so buy the sealed jar not the refill pouch.

skuLines.examples: Duphalac 100/200/450ml (lactulose), Cremaffin Plus 170/225ml, Looz syrup, Milk of Magnesia
skuLines.notes: The safe option for children, pregnancy and the elderly where a stimulant is wrong. Lactulose is prescription-classified in India — dispense against script if ARY holds a licence, and if not, this line simply cannot be carried. Heavy liquid, poor freight economics: carry the 200ml, skip the 450ml.

skuLines.examples: Glycerin suppositories (adult and paediatric), Cremalax suppository, Peglec sachet
skuLines.notes: Genuine niche for constipated infants and bed-bound elderly, and nobody else stocks it within 40 km. Suppositories soften and deform above ~25°C — in a hill store that is fine most of the year, but keep them away from winter heaters. Low volume: buy the smallest pack.

skuLines.examples: Candid 30/50g, Candid Gold 50g, Canesten 30g, Clocip 15g, Candid-B 20g (with steroid)
skuLines.seasonality: Hard Jul-Sep monsoon peak; elevated through Apr-Sep
skuLines.notes: Heavy monsoon plus shared dormitory bathrooms equals ringworm, dhobi itch and athlete's foot at scale — this is the sleeper high-volume line in a Baru Sahib planogram. Candid-B contains a steroid and is Schedule H; the plain clotrimazole is the one to push, because steroid misuse on tinea makes it worse. Counsel 4 weeks of use, not 4 days.

skuLines.examples: Ring Guard Plus 5/12/20g, Itch Guard Plus 5/12/20g, Abzorb cream, Zole-F
skuLines.notes: These are the names residents ask for, and the ₹19-23 5g tube is a real student price point. Heavily advertised, so brand pull does the selling. Stock the small tube deep and the 20g shallow — the small pack is what turns.

skuLines.examples: Abzorb dusting powder 100g, Candid dusting powder 100g, Nycil Germ Expert 150g, Dermicool, Zole-F powder
skuLines.notes: Powder beats cream for damp intertriginous areas, which is exactly the monsoon problem here. Nycil/Dermicool sit in cosmetics (no drug licence); the medicated Abzorb/Candid powders need one. Cheap, light, long shelf life — good candidate for a deep pre-monsoon buy in May.

skuLines.examples: Mediker Anti-Lice shampoo/oil 50/100ml, Licel lotion, Nix, A-Lices
skuLines.notes: A residential school with 5-18 year olds sharing dormitories will have head-lice rounds, and it spreads through a whole dorm in days. Long uncut hair in a Sikh institution makes treatment slower and repeat purchase higher. Permethrin is Schedule H; the Mediker-type shampoo is a cosmetic and sells freely. Stock a comb alongside — the comb is half the treatment.

skuLines.examples: Permite 5% 60ml, Scabper, Ascabiol, Gamma benzene hexachloride lotion
skuLines.seasonality: Outbreak-driven, winter clusters (layered clothing, shared bedding)
skuLines.notes: Prescription-only, but stock-worthy if ARY holds a licence: scabies in a dormitory is a whole-block event and treatment must cover every contact simultaneously, which means 20-40 bottles in one week, not one. Talk to the school infirmary about holding a standing reserve rather than discovering the gap mid-outbreak.

skuLines.examples: Caladryl 65/125ml, Calmac Calamine 120ml, Calapure-A 100ml, Lacto Calamine 30/60ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Sep — insect bites, prickly heat, sunburn on trek/sports days
skuLines.notes: Covers insect bites, prickly heat and allergic rash in one bottle, and most of it is cosmetic-classified so it needs no drug licence. Note Lacto Calamine is a face lotion, not a bite treatment — different shelf, different buyer, don't let the names blur in the planogram.

skuLines.examples: Hansaplast Regular 100s and Spots 250s jar, Hansaplast Antiseptic 50s jar, Hansaplast Jumbo 10s, Band-Aid Washproof, Dr. Morepen Aid 100s/150s
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 5 / 10 / 20; jar or box of 50 / 100 / 150 / 250; single loose
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks at school-session start and sports terms
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% on the pack; 40-60% when you break a 100s/250s jar and sell loose
skuLines.notes: Highest-frequency first-aid item on a school campus, and the loose-sale margin is excellent — buy the 250-count jar, sell singles at ₹2-3. Carry three formats: spot, regular strip, and jumbo/knee size. No drug licence needed (general medical device). Adhesive dries out past ~24 months, so rotate.

skuLines.line: Absorbent cotton wool roll and cotton consumables
skuLines.examples: Absorbent cotton roll 20g/125g/400g/500g, Liveasy cotton balls 50s, cotton buds 100s
skuLines.marginBand: 25-45% (commodity surgical, weak brand pull, best margin in first aid)
skuLines.notes: Both a household and an institutional line — infirmary, canteens and the clothing store all buy the 400/500g roll. Bulky and low value per kg, so this is the worst freight ratio in first aid: source from a Nahan or Solan distributor on the same truck as everything else, and buy 6 months' cover in one drop. Keep sealed; cotton wicks monsoon damp.

skuLines.line: Sterile gauze swabs and roller gauze bandage
skuLines.examples: Softswab gauze swabs 10x10cm 8-ply, sterile gauze pads 5x5 / 7.5x7.5cm, roller gauze bandage 4/6/10cm
skuLines.packSizes: swab pack of 4 / 10 / 25; roller bandage 4cm/6cm/10cm x 3-4m
skuLines.notes: Anything bigger than a band-aid needs this. Sterile packs carry an expiry on the sterility, not just the cotton — check dates, and do not sell a burst pouch. Institutional demand from the school infirmary is the steady base; household demand is spiky.

skuLines.examples: Liveasy Ortho Care crepe 8/10/15cm x 4m, Dyna crepe bandage, Flamingo elastic bandage
skuLines.seasonality: Sports terms and Nov-Feb (falls on icy/wet hill paths)
skuLines.notes: Sprained ankles are the signature injury of a hill campus with a sports programme. Stock 8cm and 10cm deep, 15cm shallow. Washable and reusable, so household repeat is slow — the volume comes from the infirmary and from new injuries, which are constant. Pairs naturally with the pain spray and the hot water bottle.

skuLines.line: Surgical tape and sterile dressing pads
skuLines.examples: 3M Micropore paper tape 1/2 inch, Leukoplast zinc oxide tape, sterile adhesive dressing pads, Liveasy corn plaster
skuLines.packSizes: tape 1.25cm / 2.5cm / 5cm x 5-9m; dressing pads 5x7 / 10x10cm, pack of 5/10
skuLines.notes: What holds the gauze on — selling gauze without tape is an incomplete basket. Micropore is the one to stock for skin that reacts to plastic tape. Small, light, long-dated: keep both widths, no reason to stock out.

skuLines.examples: St. John's / Kaptas first-aid kit, Dr. Morepen first-aid box, vehicle first-aid kit, own-assembled dorm/hostel kit
skuLines.packSizes: small household box; medium dorm/office box; vehicle kit
skuLines.marginBand: 30-50% on an own-assembled kit; 20-30% on a bought-in branded box
skuLines.notes: The highest-margin play in first aid is to assemble your own kit from lines you already stock — band-aids, gauze, tape, Betadine, cotton, paracetamol, ORS, crepe — and sell it as a priced kit to hostels, staff quarters, canteens and every campus vehicle. Institutional, repeatable, and it moves your own slow movers. Refill contracts follow.

skuLines.examples: Avomine 25mg 10s (Abbott), Vomikind MD, Domstal MD, Stemetil MD
skuLines.priceBand: ₹17-70 per strip (Avomine 10s ₹70 MRP; generic promethazine from ₹17)
skuLines.seasonality: Hard spikes at term start/end and every holiday travel window; monsoon adds nausea on a landslide-slowed road
skuLines.notes: Underrated for this specific location: 30-50 km of winding hill road means every arrival and departure is a motion-sickness event, for thousands of students several times a year. Build a spike stock ahead of the academic calendar's travel dates. Avomine causes drowsiness — say so. Domstal is Rx-restricted; Avomine and generic promethazine are the practical shelf items under a licence.

skuLines.line: Baby gripe water and colic drops
skuLines.examples: Woodward's Gripe Water 130/200ml, Colicaid drops 15/30ml, Neopeptine drops 15ml, Bonnisan liquid/drops
skuLines.notes: Married staff with infants is an explicitly named cohort here, and a colicky baby at 2am with no other shop open is exactly what a captive store exists for. Woodward's is Ayurvedic-classified and sells without Form 20/21. Never zero on this line.

skuLines.examples: Zytee RB gel, Dentogel, Mucopain gel 15g, Bonnisan teething drops
skuLines.notes: Small, cheap, and there is no substitute within 40 km. Some contain benzocaine/lignocaine and are Rx-classified — check the pack. One facing is enough, but hold it always.

skuLines.examples: Dr. Morepen / Hicks / Omron MC-246, Liveasy LET-01, Control D, BPL Accudigit DT-04, infrared non-contact
skuLines.packSizes: 1 unit boxed; digital contact and IR non-contact
skuLines.notes: Every household with children needs one and it is a one-off purchase, so demand is driven by new families and by breakage — steady, not big. Mercury thermometers are banned in Indian healthcare; stock digital only. Batteries die on the shelf: keep the button cell as a companion SKU. Carry one IR unit for the infirmary/institutional buyer.

skuLines.line: Hot water bottle and heating pad
skuLines.examples: Hicks Comfort water bag, Liveasy Ortho Care 1L/2L, Dr. Odin 1.75L/2L, Kalor rechargeable electric gel bag
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb only, and in a cold hill winter this is a strong, short, predictable season
skuLines.notes: One of the most reliably seasonal items in the store: a cold Himachal winter, an elderly cohort with joint pain, students with period cramps, and no alternative outlet. Buy in September, sell out by January, carry near-zero from March. Rubber perishes — do not carry last winter's stock into next winter and expect it not to leak.

skuLines.line: Lubricating eye drops and eye wash
skuLines.examples: Refresh Tears 10ml, Tears Naturale, Optive, Itone eye drops 10ml, sterile eye wash cup
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; dust/smoke lift in winter, conjunctivitis outbreaks in monsoon
skuLines.notes: Screen-heavy university students and dry hill winter air both drive this. Antibiotic and steroid eye drops are Rx and must not be sold loosely — sight is what gets lost. Opened bottles expire in 28 days: say it, and stock the small pack. A dormitory conjunctivitis run is an outbreak-shaped demand spike worth being ready for.

skuLines.examples: Soliwax / Waxolve / Audiclean ear drops, Clohex ear drops, Otek-AC
skuLines.notes: Small niche but there is genuinely nowhere else within 40 km. Antibiotic/steroid ear drops are Rx. Wax softeners are freely sellable and cover most of the walk-in need. One facing, no depth.

skuLines.examples: Odomos cream 25/50g, Odomos patch, Good Knight roll-on / patches, Mosquito repellent bands
skuLines.notes: Post-monsoon is dengue and vector season, and a residential campus with standing water after heavy rain is exposed. Odomos is cosmetic-classified, no drug licence. Pairs with the paracetamol/ORS block during a fever wave — merchandise them together as a monsoon shelf, which is exactly how the q-commerce players now do it.

trends2026: GST 2.0 (effective 22 Sep 2025) cut most medicines and formulations from 12% to 5% and zero-rated a list of lifesaving drugs. Printed MRPs were revised downward across the trade, so any stock still bearing a pre-Sept-2025 MRP is both a pricing error and a labelling-compliance exposure. Confidence ~85% on the rate change; the practical implication is what matters — audit printed MRP against current price lists before a big buy-in.

Generic price-anchoring has hardened. Jan Aushadhi reached 16,912 Kendras carrying 2,110 medicines and 315 devices as of 30 Jun 2025, and out-of-pocket health spend fell from 63% (FY15) to 39% (FY22). A resident who has seen a ₹4 generic paracetamol strip now prices a ₹32 Dolo 650 against it. A deliberate two-tier shelf — one brand, one generic, both visible — is now table stakes rather than a discount gimmick.

Sugar-free is the default, not the variant. Across antacid suspensions (Gelusil MPS SF, Diovol SF, Polycrol SF), cough syrups (Cofsils SF, Viscodyne SF) and lozenges, the sugar-free version is now the lead SKU on modern-trade shelves and the regular version is the tail. Reorder logic built on the old assumption over-buys the wrong pack.

Sachetisation pushed the entry price under ₹20. ₹7-10 Eno and Gas-O-Fast sachets, ₹4 4.4g ORS, ₹19-23 5g Ring Guard and Itch Guard tubes, ₹2-3 loose lozenges and band-aids. For a student and young-staff population this is where unit volume actually sits, and breaking bulk from jars and 24-packs is where the margin sits.

AYUSH-branded self-care took real share from allopathic OTC. Kadha sachets (Kofol Instant Kadha, Dabur Honitus Hot Sip), herbal cough syrups (Koflet, Zandu, Kasamrit), Ayurvedic digestives and laxatives (Pudin Hara, Zandu Nityam, Pet Saffa, Triphala) now anchor whole sub-shelves. They also carry 25-40% margin against 16-22% on scheduled drugs and sell under an Ayurvedic licence rather than Form 20/21 — the best regulation-to-margin trade in the category.

Ready-to-drink electrolyte tetrapaks migrated from the pharmacy counter to the grocery shelf and grew faster than powder, while a 2025 regulatory push against sugary drinks marketed as 'ORS' pulled the category back toward genuine WHO-formula labelling. Stock RTD shallow for convenience, keep WHO-formula sachets as the actual buffer.

Monsoon and seasonal health became a formal merchandising block, not an afterthought. PharmEasy now runs a dedicated Monsoon Store with Fungal Care, Foot Care, Kadha, Intimate Care and Mosquito Repellent as named sub-shelves — a directly copyable planogram for a heavy-monsoon hill campus, and a reminder that antifungal is a seasonal peak to pre-buy in May, not a year-round trickle.

10-minute pharmacy delivery (Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart pharma ranges, Apollo and PharmEasy express) is now normal in metros. It changes nothing operationally at Baru Sahib, but it resets the assortment expectation of students and staff returning from city trips: they expect the named brand to exist, and a bare shelf reads as a worse store than it did three years ago.
adjacentServices: A licensed retail pharmacy counter (Drugs & Cosmetics Rules Form 20/21) with a registered pharmacist on the premises. This is the gating decision for the whole category, not an add-on: without it, roughly half the lines above are illegal to sell, and the Schedule K village-shop exemption almost certainly does not cover a 5,000-resident township that has its own outlet.
Free walk-in BP, weight and temperature check at the counter. Costs one BP monitor and a chair, drives footfall from the staff and elderly cohorts, and turns a health question into a basket.
Paid blood-sugar check on a store glucometer, with strips as the consumable. Recurring revenue, and it identifies the chronic-refill customers who are worth a standing list.

Institutional first-aid kit supply and refill contract with the school wardens, hostel blocks, Eternal University, both canteens, the warehouse and every campus vehicle. Predictable monthly volume, assembled from lines already in stock at 30-50% margin, and it moves slow movers before they expire.

Prescription fulfilment tie-up with the Kalgidhar Trust hospital / campus dispensary — take their outpatient scripts rather than competing with them. This is the single largest addressable volume on campus and it needs the licensed counter to unlock.

A standing chronic-refill list for staff and elderly residents: monthly repeat packs pre-picked and reserved by name. Converts erratic walk-in demand into a forecastable order book, which is what makes buying against a 30-50 km hill supply line survivable.
Delivery to hostel blocks and staff quarters within the campus. Last-mile cost is near zero with 5,000 people in walking radius, and it is the answer for a parent with a feverish child at night.
Lab-test sample collection agency for a Nahan, Solan or Chandigarh pathology lab (Thyrocare / Dr Lal / Redcliffe franchise model). Sample goes out on the same vehicle the stock comes in on.

Medical-device rental rather than sale: nebuliser, crutches, walker, wheelchair, BP monitor, hot water bottle. Near-zero COGS after the first purchase, and it fits an injury-prone sports campus and an elderly cohort better than outright sale does.

Seasonal priced kits — a monsoon kit (ORS, antifungal cream and powder, Betadine, repellent, probiotic) and a winter kit (paracetamol, cough syrup, VapoRub, balm, lozenges, hot water bottle). Bundles lift average bill above the ₹208 baseline and pre-empt the stock-out weeks.

A formal expiry-return and breakage arrangement with the Nahan or Solan distributor / C&F. Without it, deep buffer stocking on a landslide-prone road quietly converts into write-off, which is the specific way a captive pharmacy loses money.
